# Code to disk

Copies a js file and everything it requires from the file system into an autodisk, so [disk-loader](../disk-loader) can run it straight from the disk.

Datashell uses it for the cli app: on every launch the app is copied into an autodisk and then run from there (`loadcli_drive` in `lib/datashell.js`).

Bare only, it uses `bare-module` which needs bare 1.32+.

## What it does

- Finds exactly the files the app needs, without running any of its code.
- Copies only those, a file nobody requires stays out.
- Files keep their path next to the entry file, packages from a `node_modules` folder go to `/node_modules/...` in the disk.
- Modules passed in `builtins` are not copied, they come from outside.
- Files the disk already has with the same bytes are skipped, so running it again only copies what changed.

## Usage

```javascript
const autodisk = require('autodisk')
const code_to_disk = require('code-to-disk')
const disk_loader = require('disk-loader')
const Corestore = require('corestore')
const b4a = require('b4a')

const store = new Corestore('./storage')
const drive = autodisk({ store: store.namespace('app-code') })
await drive.ready()

// copy the app into the disk, gives back where the entry file is in the disk ('/main.js')
const file = await code_to_disk({ drive, file: '/home/lupay/my-app/main.js', builtins: { b4a } })

// run it from the disk, pass the same builtins
const app = await disk_loader({ drive, file, builtins: { b4a } })
```

For an app like this:

```
my-app/
├── main.js            # require('./lib/hi.js'), require('./config.json'), require('shout'), require('b4a')
├── config.json
├── lib/
│   ├── hi.js
│   └── unused.js      # nobody requires it
└── node_modules/
    └── shout/
        ├── package.json
        └── lib/index.js
```

the disk gets `/main.js`, `/config.json`, `/lib/hi.js`, `/node_modules/shout/package.json` and `/node_modules/shout/lib/index.js`. No `unused.js` and no `b4a` (its in builtins).

## API

### await code_to_disk({ drive, file, builtins })

- `drive` - the autodisk to copy into
- `file` - path of the entry js file on the file system
- `builtins` - modules given from outside, like `{ 'bare-process': require('bare-process') }`. They are not copied. Default `{}`

Returns the path of the entry file inside the disk, which is what `disk_loader` wants as `file`.

## How it works

It uses the loader from `bare-module` (the same one disk-loader and basims packs use), but only to find the files.

**Module.Protocol** - the loader never reads files itself. It asks a protocol two things: does this url exist (`exists`) and give me its source (`read`). code-to-disk gives it a protocol that reads from the real file system and remembers every file it was asked to read. disk-loader gives it one that reads from the disk instead, thats the whole trick, same loader with a different place to read from.

**Module.Loader** - takes the protocol and the `builtins`. `defaultType: Module.constants.SCRIPT` means `.js` files are commonjs.
- `loader.link(url)` follows every `require('...')` and reads each file through the protocol, but runs nothing. code-to-disk only uses this.
- `loader.import(url)` does the same and then runs the code. disk-loader uses this.

So code-to-disk calls `link()` on the entry file, and when its done the protocol knows every file the loader needed. Those get copied into the disk.

## Things to know

- `link()` finds requires with a plain string, also ones inside functions that run later. A require with a computed name (`require(name)`) is not found, so that file isnt copied.
- A missing module doesnt stop the copy, the loader just skips it while linking. The app only fails when disk-loader runs it.
- The loader also reads the nearest `package.json` above the entry file for its settings (like the module type). If its in the entry folder it gets copied, if its above the entry folder it doesnt (it has no place in the disk).
- If a package isnt in `builtins`, its looked up in `node_modules` folders like normal and copied into the disk.

Tests: `bare lib/node_modules/code-to-disk/test.js`

For more about the loader check out https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-module
